C: › the central or main part of something where there is most activity
› the central part of a wheel into which the spokes (= bars connecting the central part to the outer edge of the wheel) are fixed

example: The City of London is the hub of the UK's financial world.
倫敦城是英國金融業的中心。
The computer department is at the hub of the company's operations.
電腦部是這家公司運作的樞紐。

NONE: › a loud noise, especially caused by a lot of people all talking at the same time
（很多人同時說話時產生的）喧嚷，喧鬧

example: I could hardly hear myself speak above all the hubbub in the bar.
在喧嚷的酒吧裡，我幾乎聽不見自己的聲音。
Once the hubbub of the election had died down, it was back to normal for the president.
一旦選舉之事塵埃落定，對於總統來說一切就恢復正常了。
She speaks fondly of Richard Moreland, hubby number one, whom she still sees regularly.
她說起理查‧莫蘭德——她的第一任丈夫時，仍一往情深，到現在還經常跟他見面。

NONE: › the circular metal covering over the hub of a vehicle's wheel
› a way of talking or behaving that is too proud

example: He was punished for his hubris.
他因為自大而受到懲罰。
